request.spec:
A grade merge is now retroactive: for every person it moves, every grade record of theirs on the
merged grade becomes the other grade, so all their claims, whatever their date, use the other
grade's rates (and its terms and thresholds) from then on. Frozen figures and figures bound by a
statement are unchanged.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A grade merge is now retroactive: for every person it moves, every grade record of theirs on the
merged grade becomes the other grade, so all their claims, whatever their date, use the other
grade's rates (and its terms and thresholds) from then on. Frozen figures and figures bound by a
statement are unchanged.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A grade merge is now retroactive. `bin/e2e` passes 3 of the 4 tests. The fourth, "scenario 1", fails because of a mistake in the spec itself, not in the app.

**The change** (server only; no schema or front-end change was needed):
- `Person.java`: a new `regrade(from, into)` method changes every grade record a person has on the merged grade to the other grade. That includes the grade they started with and every later dated one.
- `GradeMergeService.java`: each person the merge moves is still edited as before, which gives them the new grade from today. Then `regrade` is applied to them and saved, before the merge's closing rollup audit.

All of a moved person's claims, whatever their date, now use the other grade's rates, terms and thresholds. Frozen figures and figures bound by a statement are unchanged. The audit file gets exactly the lines the spec expects.

**The failing test:** at line 243, the spec sets the sheet parent to `${sheet}-p` (line 135) but then checks for the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That looks like a placeholder that never got filled in, so no correct app can pass that check. I didn't edit the spec, as the rules require. To check the rest of that test, I ran a temporary copy with only that one line changed to `sheet + "-p"`, and it passed in full. I then deleted the copy. Someone needs to fix that line in the spec before `bin/e2e` can pass all four tests.
